findings.problem: On its own, 'meist' is the adverb 'usually, mostly', and a subtitle token 'meist' is almost always that adverb, because the determiner 'most' always has an ending (meiste, meisten), so the card teaches the wrong meaning for this word.
findings.fix: kind: content; pos: adverb; en: usually, mostly; hint: the short word, not meistens or normalerweise

findings.problem: The natural answer for '[most] of my friends' is 'die meisten', and the hint asks for a 'base form' meist that never appears without an ending in this meaning, so the learner is told to recall a form German doesn't use here.
findings.fix: en: usually, mostly; hint: the short word, not meistens or normalerweise

findings.problem: For the determiner, 'meist' is not the dictionary form, which would be 'meiste' (der/die/das meiste, die meisten); bare 'meist' is only right as the adverb.
findings.fix: Keep target: meist, with pos: adverb and grammar: null

findings.problem: The sentence is correct German but uses the determiner 'die meisten', not the adverb 'meist' that this word is.
findings.fix: example.target: Ich fahre meist mit dem Rad zur Arbeit. example.en: I usually cycle to work.

back.target: usually, mostly (adverb; the determiner 'most' is always inflected: der/die/das meiste, die meisten)
back.example: Most of my friends live in Berlin.

note: The trick (meist rhymes with iced and sounds like most) still works for the adverb card, e.g. 'most of the time = meist'; it is a short synonym of the more common 'meistens', which is why the hint has to rule that word out.
